Typical causes for AUTH-403 include account lockout, expired or invalid credentials/tokens, permission changes, or IP/security policy restrictions.

Hello Enterprise Client 1,

Thank you for reaching out about the AUTH‑403 error you’re seeing when trying to access the dashboard. I’m sorry for the inconvenience this has caused.

We’ve taken the following steps on our side:
• Verified your identity using the email address and phone number we have on file.
• Checked the authentication registry and confirmed that your account is active (it was not locked or disabled).
• Generated a secure, self‑service password‑reset link that will expire in 15 minutes. This link has been sent to your registered email address.

To restore access, please:
1. Click the password‑reset link in the email and follow the prompts to set a new password.
2. After resetting, clear your browser’s cookies and cache, or open a private/incognito browsing window, then attempt to log in again.
3. If you still encounter the AUTH‑403 error, please reply with the IP address you are using so we can verify that there are no IP‑allowlist or geographic restrictions affecting your login.

If you have any questions or need further assistance, don’t hesitate to let us know.

Best regards,
Customer Support Team
